items.title: Interpretable Factor Decomposition for Decision Intelligence in Large-Scale Financial Markets: Evidence from China's A-Share Market
items.relevance: XGBoost + TreeSHAP attribution on 3,632 China A-share stocks; behavioral signals (turnover + momentum) account for 58.2% of predictive attribution vs 10.7% for valuation ratios. Corroborates our own repeated finding across H198/H217/H228/H411-H418 that momentum dominates other factor families on the strategies we've tested, but is a China A-share study (different market microstructure, T+1 settlement, price limits) — not staged as an actionable proposal, just noted here for the record. Below the bar for a wiki note since it doesn't add a new mechanism, only corroborates an already well-established wiki finding.

items.title: Machine Learning Enhanced Multi-Factor Quantitative Trading: A Cross-Sectional Portfolio Optimization Approach with Bias Correction
items.relevance: documents a 'mask-first' tradability-bias fix (non-tradable price contamination in rolling-window factor calcs) with a quantified -0.44 Sharpe / +18% inflated-IC impact when the mask is absent. Generalizable look-ahead-bias hygiene lesson beyond its China-specific price-limit context — staged as a methodology audit lead for our own run_hNNN.py scripts.
